answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly assign tasks and have independent peers verify results. If several identities collude, they still must fund each slot; detected duplicate submissions or provable fraud burn the stake. This raises the cost of a Sybil swarm from cheap account creation to capital at risk, while random assignment limits its ability to control a whole trellis, terrace, or echo of reviewers.
